messages:
ara: quick heads-up — I rolled out an experiment for prod-chat: p95 SLO = 220ms, dynamic token budgets by route/tier. Goal: cut tail by doing an early-batch cutoff when queue depth > 12 and lower token budget for low-tier routes.

josh: nice. what's the exact cutoff logic?

ara: logic is simple for now — when queue_len > 12 we do: max_tokens = min(default, floor(token_budget * 0.6)) for tier=free; for tier=paid we keep token_budget. Also we pick kernel_prefetch=true for short sequences to avoid kernel-switch overhead. config snippet: 
```
batcher: 
  early_cutoff: {threshold: 12, action: reduce_token_budget} 
routes: 
  prod-chat: {p95_target_ms: 220, tiers: {free: 0.6, paid: 1.0}} 
kernel: 
  prefetch_short_seqs: true
```

maria: hmm we need to be careful — KV cache hit behavior can change effective latency if we shrink max_tokens. Did you profile KV misses?

ara: yes i ran a quick profiler on a 2h window. runtime-bot gave a summary.

runtime-bot: profile: prod-chat experiment 1797654321 -> 1797654520; samples=14k. p50=48ms p95=238ms p99=430ms. kv_cache_hit_rate change: -4.2% on free-tier traffic. kernel-switches per request: down 18% for short seqs.

josh: p95 went up to 238ms? that's >220 target. Where is the regression?

ara: the regression is mostly on requests with mid-length responses (seq 150-350 tokens). We cut token budget which forced more frequent micro-batching boundaries and dropped effective batching density for those requests — plus KV misses. Full breakdown:
- short (<64): p95 improved by ~12ms
- mid (150-350): p95 worsened by ~40ms
- long (>800): unchanged

maria: that suggests our early cutoff is too blunt. Maybe use token-budget scaling based on queued-weighted token distributions, not just queue length. Eg compute avg_pending_tokens for last 20 reqs and scale.

sam: also consider a grace window to allow KV-prefetch to warm up. If a route has many small edits, reducing tokens hurts KV efficacy. Could tag routes with kv_prefetch_priority.

ara: agreed. next iteration: replace scalar threshold with a score = queue_len * avg_pending_tokens / gpu_slots. If score > X then reduce free-tier budget by factor f(score). Also add route-level kv_prefetch_priority and an observability counter.

josh: can you drop the new config so SRE and perf can run a canary? I want to see microbatch occupancy graphs and kernel-switch traces for mid-length traffic.

ara: dropping now to canary cluster canary-3; will push config and run 30m windows. runtime-bot will post perf summary.

runtime-bot: deploy: canary-3 config v12 pushed at 1797654501. will collect 30m window starting 1797654560. tracing: enabled for mid-length route samples @ 10% sampling.

maria: for the scoring function, prefer exponential smoothing for avg_pending_tokens so spikes don't overreact. alpha=0.2 seemed stable in earlier tests.

sam: also add a small hysteresis on budget changes to avoid flip-flopping when load oscillates (min_hold_sec=8).

ara: noted: smoothing alpha=0.2, hysteresis=8s, score formula added, kv_prefetch_priority tag. launching.

josh: post the profile dump here when ready. focus on: batch density (tokens per GPU), kernel-switch counts, kv-hit delta, and p95 by length-bucket.

runtime-bot: profiling results 30m canary window (1797654560-1797656360):
- overall p95=221ms (improved vs 238), p50=50ms, p99=412ms
- free-tier kv_hit_rate delta = -1.3% (much better than -4.2)
- mid-length p95 now +3ms vs baseline (acceptable)
- microbatch occupancy improved +9% for mid-length traffic
- kernel-switch count reduced 11%

maria: that's promising. small regressions at mid-length but within noise. we still need to verify stability under a 2h sustained load.

ara: agree. next step: promote to extended canary (2h) and enable full tracing for a 1% sample to inspect token fragmentation patterns and KV ages.

sam: also add an alert rule: if mid-length p95 > 260ms for >5m rollback automatically.

josh: one more idea — for mid-length we might prefer a smaller token reduction factor but also allow one extra microbatch slot (burst slot) to accommodate tails. Could be cheaper than regressing throughput.

ara: good point. will add burst_slot: 1 for paid, 0 for free initially. adding to canary v13.

runtime-bot: canary v13 pushed at 1797654680. extended window start 1797654700.

ara: thanks all — i'll post final 2h report but initial numbers look like the scoring+prefetch tags fixed most of the regression. we still need runbook updates. :thumbsup:
